provenance: Sir Herbert Frederick Cook, 3rd Baronet (1868-1939); Sir Francis Cook, 4th Baronet (1907-1978), and by descent. The present portrait is known in numerous versions, one of which hung at Althorp, Northamptonshire. Doughty House is a substantial, Grade II listed 18th Century house on Richmond Hill overlooking the Thames. From 1849 it was the home of the Cook family and housed their important collection of paintings, but it suffered bomb damage during WW2 and Sir Francis Cook, 4th Baronet, moved to Jersey in 1948 with some of the paintings. The house was sold in 2013. The frame of this painting bears the number 400 relating to the numbering of the Doughty House collection.

artwork_title: Portrait of Troiano Marulli, 3rd Duke of Ascoli
provenance: With Albert Heyse, Ghent. This portrait of Troiano Marulli, 3rd Duke of Ascoli, can be identified as the original life study of around 1822 - 23 for van Hanselaer's full length portrait now in the Pio Monte della Misericordia in Naples. Among the orders the Duke is shown wearing are that of S. Giorgio della Riunione, San Ferdinando e del Merito and those of Leopold of Austria and of Charles III of Spain. Van Henselaer was a Belgian artist who served as a court artist to the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies from 1822 until 1828 when he returned home to Ghent. An old label on the reverse of the painting indicating that it was loaned to the Ghent state museum suggests that Van Henselaer retained this work in his own collection, reflecting the high quality of the study. Subsequently it was in the collection of the early 20th century Ghent dealer and collector Albert Heyse.

The subject he chose was that of Resurrection, featuring the apotheosis of the founder of the college, Archbishop Henry Chichele (c.1364-1443). The presentation design, which is more finished and varies from the present drawing, is in the collection of the Ashmolean Museum, Oxford (WA2002.26).
